title: feat(security)!: an anonymous caller never owns a record and never sets its owner (ADR-0138 E3)
body:
Fixes #23226
Clause-②: no (narrowing) — a guest-supplied owner is refused at the endpoints and the owner column never holds the guest or the system principal. That tightens what a guest write may carry and admits nothing refused today.

ADR-0138 **E3**, D1 ("the guest is a principal, never an owner"). This lands the guest branch of the owner-anchor stamp in `SecurityPlugin`, which the record names as D1's enforcement point. Claim `6157234533`, branch `claude/issue-23226-guest-owner-stamp`. ⛔ Nothing in the record is re-decided. One measurement departs from D1 outside the stamp. It is raised to the seat, not decided here (see **Raised, not decided**).

## What changed (`@objectstack/plugin-security` only)

- **Step 3.5, the guest branch.** It applies to the guest envelope (`principalKind: 'guest'`, no `userId`):
  - Nothing is stamped. An absent owner stays unset. An empty-string owner is also left unset; it used to be stored as an empty string.
  - A guest-supplied owner is refused with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, on insert and on update (a transfer, a disown or an echo), **whatever the guest holds**. The transfer grant is never consulted for a guest, and the refusal names no grant to acquire.
  - Callers with a user id keep the stamp and the forge rule unchanged.
- **One reader of the guest fact.** A module-level `isGuestEnvelope` holds E1's own predicate (`principalKind === 'guest' && !userId`). The set resolution (E1, D3) and the organization refusal (E1, D4) now call it too, instead of keeping two inline copies. This adds no new guest predicate, and `plugin-sharing`'s module-private `isGuestPrincipal` is not reused.
- **The `publicFormGrant` branch** is unchanged. It gains a one-line ADR-0138 D1 note.
- The diff stays clear of the regions #23334 changed (the catalog-echo registration and the `kernel:ready` pass). #23334 merged first, and `main` is merged in (`ab5209be3f`), with no conflict.

## Measured on `bbb9757717`, before the change (the PM's H1 to H4)

- **H1. What a guest write stored at the doors E1 opened.**
  - **Class-4 endpoint door** (`authRequired: false`, `type: 'object_operation'`):
    - With no owner supplied, no owner was stored. The stamp writes `userId` only when one is present.
    - A supplied empty string was stored as an empty string.
    - A supplied owner was refused only because the guest lacked the transfer grant. When the guest's bound set carried the transfer bit, the forged owner was stored: a real user's id, and also the system principal's `usr_system` (present as a legacy row).
    - The anchor tier refuses that bit at every binding door, so no binding a deployment can make today reached this.
  - **Class-5 flow door:**
    - A `runAs: 'user'` flow is refused before its data node reaches the engine. That is already pinned by `declarative-endpoint-anonymous-guest.dogfood.test.ts`.
    - A `runAs: 'system'` flow bypasses the middleware (see Acceptance notes).
- **H2. Held.** The guest fact is E1's predicate, factored into one reader.
- **H3. Held, by order.**
  - A `beforeInsert` hook runs inside `engine.insert`'s operation, after the middleware chain: `triggerHooks('beforeInsert')` sits in the executor that `executeWithMiddleware` wraps.
  - A record-change flow is its own write.
  - No middleware registered ahead of the security middleware writes `owner_id`.
  - So any `owner_id` on a guest write's payload at step 3.5 arrived with that write. "Supplied" and "set by the scenario" are told apart by where the value came from, never by its content.
- **H4. Held.** `PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS` carries `owner_id`. The form route's filter and the `publicFormGrant` strip both drop it, and the form row stays unowned. `packages/spec` is untouched.
- **Assignment rules.** The platform has no first-class assignment-rule mechanism (zero source hits). An assignment rule is written as a hook or a record-change flow, the two writers pin 2 exercises.

## Pins, each with a negative control

| Row clause | Pin | Negative control |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1. A guest insert with nothing setting an owner leaves it unset | dogfood, class-4 door: the stored owner is null, for an absent owner, a `null` owner and an empty-string owner. Unit: nothing is stamped, and empty owners are left null | Control: a signed-in caller's row on the same object is stamped with its own id. Mutation leg B (the stamp writes the system principal for a guest) turns pin 1 red |
| 2. An owner set by a hook, flow or assignment rule stands | dogfood: a code-registered `beforeInsert` hook's owner and a `runAs: 'system'` record-change flow's owner both stand on the guest's row | Control: the plain object's guest row, with no writer, is unset, so the owner comes from the scenario's writer. Under leg B the hook and the flow still win, and the no-writer control turns red |
| 3. A guest-supplied owner is refused at an endpoint and stripped at the form doors | dogfood: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (code and status), and no row lands, with a plain set and with a transfer-bit set (the set is checked against `describeAnchorForbiddenBits` and refused). The form door strips a submitted owner. Unit: refused for create-only, transfer-bit and modify-all guests, three forged owners each, batch rows, and updates | Controls: the same guest and the same grant with no owner are admitted. A caller with the transfer authority sets the same owner on the same object, the form object included. Leg A turns the transfer-bit pin red |
| 4. The owner column never holds the guest or the system principal | dogfood: a guest naming `usr_system` or `guest` as owner is refused despite the transfer bit. A census of every guest-written row finds only null or the scenario's user | Legs A and B both turn it red |

## Ablation

The fix was committed first (`3e44b3d5ee`). Each leg ran through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode, with a `trap` restore. Each leg rebuilt `plugin-security` and ran `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs` before reading any result. No ablation file is kept.

| Leg | Mutation (anchor hit 1, blob changed) | dist reading | Unit (guest branch, 5) | Dogfood (13) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A: remove the guest branch | `const guest = isGuestEnvelope(opCtx.context);` becomes `const guest = false;` | `--absent`: marker gone from all 6 built files, tree on the mutate leg | **4 red**: the empty owner is kept as `''`, and the transfer-bit and modify-all guests are admitted on insert, batch and update | **4 red**: the empty owner reads `expected '' to be null`, pin 3 transfer-bit and pin 4 read `expected 201 to be 403`, and the census finds 8 guest rows instead of 7 |
| B: the stamp writes the system principal for a guest | `else if (guest) row.owner_id = 'usr_system';` | present in `index.js` and `index.mjs` | **3 red** | **5 red**: pin 1 reads `expected 'usr_system' to be null` (three rows), the pin 2 control and the census fail |
| R: restore | blob `0ce005f6ed` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, porcelain is empty | `isGuestEnvelope(opCtx.context)` present again, and leg B's marker `--absent` | 5/5 | 13/13 |

**The direction observed, as it fell.**
- Removing the guest branch does **not** turn pin 1's absent-owner case red. The stamp's existing `if (userId)` guard already writes nothing for a caller with no user id, so that case has no guest-specific code to remove.
- Its teeth are mutation leg B instead, and the member control.
- Leg A turns red the clauses that depend on the branch: the empty owner, pin 3 with the transfer bit, and pin 4.

With 14 neighbouring suites (guest grants, anonymous endpoint, endpoint policy, owner anchor and bulk writes, the public form suites, seed-ownership claim, anonymous door sweep, authz conformance, showcase anonymous deny, form self-auth): 15 files, 162 passed.
  - `typecheck` is 0 errors, and `--listFiles` includes the new file.
- **ESLint, as a proven narrowing:**
  - `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 3 changed `.ts` files: 3 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, at `ab5209be3f`.
  - The population is the root `eslint.config.mjs`'s `**/*.{ts,...}` block, and no file was reported ignored.
  - Invariance: that config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`, no typed rules, per its own header), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.
  - The full `pnpm lint` is CI's.

## Gates

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, at `ab5209be3f`: 70 commands, all exit 0.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, because 8 unrelated packages had no `dist/`. Those were built, and it re-ran green.
- `--ran` reconciliation: "70 derived, 70 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", "a DERIVED zero — all 70 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3".
- `check:adr-0087-registration`: "✓ check-adr-0087-registration: 1 declared-breaking changeset(s), each carrying an ADR-0087 disposition." The marker reads `.changeset/23226-guest-owner-stamp.md [BREAKING+bang+clause-②-narrowing] not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, which is the record row's "none: no new key, and nothing moves".
- Labels: the dispatch names none, and `skip-changeset` does not apply (the package publishes). Zero label writes.

## Raised, not decided

**The seed-settle claim hands guest-written rows to the platform admin.**
- What happens: `SecurityPlugin.claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` runs `claimSeedOwnership` on every `app:seeded`, which fires on every boot whose app declares seed data. It re-owns every row of a user-authored object whose `owner_id` is null (or `usr_system`) to the platform admin. Its predicate cannot tell a seed row from a guest-written or form-door row.
- Measured on a booted stack (a scratch probe, not committed): a guest row and a form-door row, both unowned, became the platform admin's after one `app:seeded`. The log line read `handed 2 seeded record(s) to platform admin`.
- The record says otherwise:
  - D1 item 3: "The platform stamps nothing on a guest insert and declares no organization-level default owner".
  - D1 item 5: "a guest-written row keeps no owner, exactly as the public form doors' intake does today". The form doors' rows are claimed the same way today.
- This sits outside the stamp, the record's named enforcement point, and nothing in this diff depends on how it is answered. The question and its options are in the `os-dev-report` comment on #23226.

## Acceptance notes

- **The class-5 flow door under `runAs: 'system'`.** Until D2b's publish refusal lands (card E2), such a flow writes as the system principal. That bypasses the middleware, this branch included. The row's owner is whatever the flow's nodes set, and a node can map a request input into `owner_id`. Carrier: E2's card.
- **The ADR anchor registry.** `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin.ts.json` lists ADR-0055, ADR-0106 and ADR-0123. ADR-0138 is cited in the code at each site but is not added to the registry, which is outside the claim's file surface. Carrier: none.
- **File surface, against the claim.** All edits are in the claimed `security-plugin.ts`: step 3.5, E1's `:6486` read and its D4 refusal read (now through the one reader), and a comment in the `publicFormGrant` branch. The rest is its tests (a unit block in `security-plugin.test.ts`, and the dogfood file) and one changeset.
